text:
[LCST.4.5.8] **`String → Float` accepted inputs.** `x::Float?` parses a string
that is, in its entirety, an optional sign (`+` or `-`) followed by either an
`INT_LIT` ([LLEX.11.1]) or a `FLOAT_LIT` ([LLEX.11.2]), with `_` separators
placed as a source literal may place them, or by `inf`. The runtime must yield
the value rounded to the nearest `Float`, ties to even ([LDET.3.2.7]); a zero
keeps the sign it is spelt with, as an `INT_LIT` (`-0`, `-0x0`) or a
`FLOAT_LIT` (`-0.0`) alike, and `inf` with its sign yields that infinity. It must yield
`null` for every other string: a finite spelling whose value rounds to an
infinity, one with any surrounding whitespace, a unit suffix, a NaN spelling,
or any spelling a source literal would not admit.

Every canonical rendering of a `Float` ([LCST.4.5.6]) is accepted here, so a
`Float → String → Float` round trip returns the value it started from.

alloy.name: lcst_4_5_8__parse_yields_no_nan
alloy.note: The parse as a source of Float operands: the accepted spellings denote a finite value or `inf`, and 'a NaN spelling' is among the strings that yield `null`, which is no operand. What [NDET.1.4]'s signalling-NaN exclusion takes from this clause.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_8__negative
idris.note: Whether the text opens with a `-`: the sign of the clause's optional sign.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_8__null_spellings
idris.note: The sixteen texts of LCST.4.5.8_float_non_literals_are_null parse to nothing, each `Refl` and each decided before a double is built: the NaN spellings, surrounding whitespace, a unit suffix with and without its `_`, one side of the point, a bare exponent marker, a hex float, `1e400` (past the largest double, by its digit count), a separator beside the point, the empty text, and an integer spelling outside the 64-bit range ([LLEX.11.1.5]).

idris.name: lcst_4_5_8__parse_float
idris.note: The clause: the whole text an optional sign then an `INT_LIT` in the 64-bit range, a `FLOAT_LIT` or `inf`, to the nearest double, ties to even ([LDET.3.2.8]), a zero keeping the sign it is spelt with as an `INT_LIT` (`-0`, `-0x0`) or a `FLOAT_LIT` (`-0.0`) alike, as the clause states, `inf` with its sign the infinity, and `null` for every other text -- a spelling that rounds past the largest double, whitespace, a unit suffix, a NaN spelling, any spelling a source literal would not admit. logical/LCST.4.5.8_signed_zero_in_every_base spells the zero in every base and agrees with libds under idris-libds. The rounding is exact Integer arithmetic, run and not proved.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_8__parse_is_a_value_or_null
idris.note: `s :: Float?` is a Float or `null` for every text, never a trap: the clause's two `must`s have no third outcome.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_8__unsigned
idris.note: The text after the clause's optional sign, `+` or `-`.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_8__of_decimal
idris.note: A signed decimal to the nearest double, ties to even, a zero keeping its spelt sign: the magnitude settled by the digit count before any arithmetic -- past `10^310` nothing, the clause's `null` for a finite spelling that rounds to an infinity; below `10^-324` the signed zero -- and `ldet_3_2_8__nearest` between. Run, not proved.

idris.name: llex_11_2__accepted_spellings
idris.note: The seven `FLOAT_LIT` spellings of LCST.4.5.8_float_formats_parse read to their decimals, each `Refl` (`1500.0`, `1.5e3`, `1.5E3`, `1.5e+03`, `15e2`, `1_500.0` as 1500, and `1e1_0`, a separator in an exponent); the fixture's integer spellings take the `INT_LIT` path.
